messages:
alex: Morning team, I'm handing off — leaving the cluster in steady state. Notes below, pls read before taking oncall.

alex: Handoff bullet points:
- Postmortem action RED-3421 (cache eviction tuning) rolled in canary last night (release v1.12.3-canary).
- We saw reduced tail latency in tests but one regression on small-batch qps around 03:10 UTC (root cause: batch-router backoff miscount).
- I pushed a hotfix to routing that patches the miscount; canary redeploy is in progress.
- Follow-up: QA to validate request/response shape for pinned routing and mark RED-3421 as verified.

maria: Thanks Alex. I'll take the next shift. pinging @li for QA verification. Is there a simple curl to check the canary?

alex: Yep, use the canary header and the health endpoints. Example:
```bash
curl -s -H \"x-redwood-canary: true\" \
  https://api-canary.redwood.internal/v1/infer -d '{"input":"hello"}' | jq '.latency, .ok'
```
Expect `.ok == true` and latency < 200ms for short prompts.

li: On it, starting smoke tests now. I will run three workloads: small-batch, long-seq, and concurrent-embed.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: v1.12.3-canary - 1859009985 by alex :white_check_mark:

li: Small-batch test: reproduces the slight qps dip but after hotfix it's within acceptable variance. Long-seq looks stable. Concurrent embed flakiness still shows 2% 5xx for a 10m window. Logging into logs to see traces.

sam: Do we want to open RED-3421-2 for the embed flakiness or keep under the existing ticket? Postmortem action 3.2 said to \"verify no regressions on embed path.\"

maria: Let's create a subtask under RED-3421 (RED-3421-2) so it's trackable. li, can you capture trace IDs and attach? I'll assign to infra-runtime.

li: Will collect traces and attach. Preliminary trace shows redis timeout spikes around the same window — might be a transient network blip. I ran the following to pull traces:
```bash
rg 'trace_id' /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 50
```
I'll paste the trace IDs in the ticket.

alex: Thanks. Also note: if you see fallbacks to model-small-2, don't panic — routing fallback is expected when a host returns 503. The important part is to confirm there are no silent tokenization mismatches.

maria: li, once you attach traces, I can mark RED-3421 as \"in validation\". If traces point to infra (redis/network), we'll reassign.

li: Uploaded traces and notes to RED-3421-2. Two suspicious redis timeouts (ID: trace-20260317-7a1f, trace-20260317-7a2b).

sam: Quick question: are we enabling automatic rollback for canary if error rate > 1%? The policy in console says rollback at 2% by default.

alex: Console policy is 2%. I lowered it to 1% for this canary night due to prior postmortem sensitivity. I left a comment in the deploy.

maria: OK. I'll monitor for the next 30m and will escalate if error rate crosses 1%. li, if you confirm infra cause, we probably close without reopen. If it's app-level, we'll reopen the postmortem.

li: Infra looks intermittent, marking RED-3421-2 as infra-owned. Leaving remediation status: validating fix; will follow up with logs in 1h.

maria: Great. Thanks everyone — I have the handoff. alex, enjoy your break. :slightly_smiling_face:

alex: Thanks, team. ping me if anything spikes. :raised_hands:
